clue.text: Firm provision for retirement?

parts.note: read as a company's arrangement to pay staff after they stop working, a fixed pot of money set aside

explanation.surface: A question about how solidly someone has planned for their old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' seems to mean secure, but it is the company that makes the provision.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies run such a scheme to pay employees an income once they stop working.

clue.text: Leading churchmen ringing hypocritically virtuous drug suppliers

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the churchmen surround the other piece

parts.note: popes are the heads of the Catholic church
pi is crossword slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Senior clergy surrounding sanctimonious people who deal in narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Opium is made from the poppy, which is why the flowers count as drug suppliers.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium and its derivatives are made from the seed heads of these flowers.

clue.text: Is one variety of aural distraction

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something is one kind of distracting sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted sound is something heard that pulls attention away.

clue.text: Neither here nor there, apparently

parts.note: the idiom for irrelevant is read literally: not at the start point nor at the destination, but travelling between

explanation.surface: Something dismissed as irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people still travelling are at neither their starting place nor their destination.

clue.text: One doesn't have to have it

definitions.text: One doesn't have to have it

parts.words: One doesn't have to have it
parts.note: read the opposite way: a person who lacks something is the one who requires it

explanation.surface: A statement that something is optional.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the thing is optional; the cryptic reading is that the person who 'doesn't have' it is the one in want.
explanation.definitionFit: A want or requirement is felt by someone who lacks the thing wanted.

clue.text: Where you can't go in a bungalow

definitions.text: Where you can't go in a bungalow

parts.words: Where you can't go in a bungalow
parts.note: a bungalow is a single-storey house, so there is no higher floor to climb to

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place off limits in a one-floor home.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-storey house has no first floor to climb to.

clue.text: I held out for foreign capital

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these words are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resisted pressure from overseas investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held out' reads as resisted and 'capital' as money, but 'out' is the anagram signal and the capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of India, a foreign country to a British solver.

clue.text: The character in "The Merry Wives of Windsor" least like Falstaff

definitions.text: The character in "The Merry Wives of Windsor" least like Falstaff

parts.words: The character in "The Merry Wives of Windsor" least like Falstaff
parts.note: Falstaff is famously fat; one of the play's characters is named for being thin

explanation.surface: A question about Shakespeare's comedy and its fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham Slender is a foolish suitor in the play; his name also means thin, the opposite of the fat Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a minor suitor in the play is also a word for thin, unlike the corpulent knight.

clue.text: Why a note might by synonymous with 3, possibly

definitions.text: Why a note might by synonymous with 3, possibly

parts.words: Why a note might by synonymous with 3, possibly
parts.note: spell the word for a road: the letter A, a musical note, sits after the W; and the phrase means travelling, like clue 3

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about notes and synonyms.
explanation.walkthrough: In W-A-Y the note A follows W; the whole phrase also means travelling, as clue 3 (in transit) does.
explanation.definitionFit: Being en route means still travelling, the same as being between departure and arrival.

clue.text: Blunt to no purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a sharp tip, and also futile or meaningless.

clue.text: A boy meaning to do surgical work

definitions.meaning: to cut open a boil or abscess with a blade

explanation.surface: A youngster who intends to become a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, and a verb for piercing an abscess with a scalpel.

clue.text: He has to dispose of his frozen assets to survive

definitions.text: He has to dispose of his frozen assets to survive

parts.words: He has to dispose of his frozen assets to survive
parts.note: frozen assets is read literally: the man's stock is blocks of ice, which he sells for a living

explanation.surface: A businessman forced to liquidate locked-up funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frozen assets' is financial jargon for money that cannot be touched; here it is literal ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who delivered blocks of ice made his living selling frozen stock.

clue.text: Is he among the players in exile?

indicators.note: among means placed amid, so these words go inside the group

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: A question whether some man is in the line-up of a team in exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sent away from their homeland and forbidden to return is exiled.

clue.text: He loves causing cruel suffering but is sorrowful first

parts.note: sorrowful means sad
1st is the usual abbreviation for first, read as IST

explanation.surface: A tormentor who is nevertheless unhappy to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of '1st' is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others.

clue.text: A story that isn't generally told

definitions.text: A story that isn't generally told

parts.words: A story that isn't generally told
parts.note: not generally is read as not in broad outline, so the narrative goes into every particular

explanation.surface: A secret tale not widely known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' suggests 'widely', but it means 'in general terms': the story is told in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A full report gives every particular instead of a summary.

clue.text: Big fight for the championship of Europe

definitions.text: Big fight for the championship of Europe

parts.words: Big fight for the championship of Europe
parts.note: a title bout in boxing is read as the 1914-18 conflict between European powers for dominance

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxing bout for the European title.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is boxing; the answer is the First World War, a struggle for mastery of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1914-18 conflict was a huge struggle among European powers for supremacy.

clue.text: Man of mixed race out of place on a safari

indicators.note: out of place means disarranged, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who looks out of place on an African safari.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated term describes a person of combined African and Asian descent.

clue.text: Sort of people who can afford to do nothing

definitions.text: Sort of people who can afford to do nothing

parts.words: Sort of people who can afford to do nothing
parts.note: wealthy people with no need to work and so spend their days lazing

explanation.surface: A description of the leisured class.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people who need no job may spend their time in leisure.

clue.text: What one must have to be fit for work

definitions.text: What one must have to be fit for work

parts.words: What one must have to be fit for work
parts.note: fit is read as suited rather than healthy: a natural talent for a job

explanation.surface: A question about the health needed for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' suggests physical health; here it means suited, as by natural ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or ability is what makes a person suited to a task.

clue.text: See 14
A breakwater in which no grey is to be seen

indicators.note: the words are to be seen in another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea wall with no grey stone visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which ... is to be seen' signals that the letters of 'no grey' are rearranged to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall built out from a beach into the sea to check erosion.

clue.text: Home of our least affluent capitalists?

definitions.text: Home of our least affluent capitalists?

parts.words: Home of our least affluent capitalists?
parts.note: capitalists is read as residents of the capital, London, and the poorest live in one district

explanation.surface: A question about where the poorest financiers live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalists' suggests investors but means Londoners; the EAST END is London's traditionally poor district by the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: London's traditionally working-class district lies east of the City, near the docks.

clue.text: Renowned old Indian governor with retreat near Maidenhead

definitions.text: Renowned old Indian governor with retreat near Maidenhead

parts.note: Robert Clive, Clive of India, governed Bengal in the eighteenth century
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A colonial grandee with a country bolt-hole in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIVEDEN is a famous country house on the Thames near Maidenhead, a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The stately house on the Thames in Berkshire is a famous country retreat.

clue.text: Relieved of a seed, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible other form of these words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone freed of a pip or kernel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain or stress that has lessened is alleviated.

clue.text: It turns in to approve of a drink that is popular in France

definitions.text: a drink that is popular in France

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the verb for approve

parts.note: to pass a measure is to approve it

indicators.note: turns means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone changing their mind to endorse a favourite French drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It turns' looks like a whole phrase about changing your mind, but 'turns' only acts on 'It'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured aperitif drunk widely in the south of France.

clue.text: Luggage vehicles now out of fashion

definitions.meaning: light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriages, no longer used

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned luggage carriages no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for belongings, and old pony carts of the horse-drawn era.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of plant life

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
the main stalk holding up leaves and flowers

explanation.surface: A loyal backer of botany.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt a flow, and the stalk bearing a plant's leaves and flowers.

clue.text: They employ 27 ruses

indicators.note: the answer to 27 across means complicated, so the letters of the following word are tangled

explanation.surface: People who make use of complicated tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 27 is the answer to 27 across, used as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who make use of something are its consumers.

clue.text: Having complexity can make it certain

indicators.note: can make says the letters of these words can be rebuilt into another word

explanation.surface: A claim that complexity can create certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with many detailed interlocking parts is elaborate.

clue.text: Impersonal description of a fully automated set-up?

definitions.text: Impersonal description of a fully automated set-up?

parts.words: Impersonal description of a fully automated set-up?
parts.note: a factory run by machines has had its human staff removed, which also means made inhuman

explanation.surface: A cold way of describing a robot factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means stripped of human qualities, and literally a works with its people taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped of human warmth, and also having had all human workers taken out.
